label: paragraph_title
text: YESTERDAY'S CLUB VICTORY

label: text
text:
By 5 goals to 8, the Hongkong Hockey Club 1st XI defeated the Punjab Regiment 1st XI at the U.S.R.C. ground, Kowloon, yesterday, after an enjoyable match.
With the Club forwards passing in excellent style yesterday Evans shot two goals in the first half, the second being a beautiful effort.
There was no more scoring until after half time when the Punjabis reduced the deficit to 2-1. Then Woodward found the mark, the ball going in off the Punjab goalkeeper's stick. When about three-quarters of the game had been played, Lt. Wright-Neville, playing centre forward for the soldiers, scored two goals, leveling the score at 3 all.
A nice shot by Woodward gave the Club the lead again (4-3) and Allen obtained a lovely last goal.

label: paragraph_title
text: Comment On Game.

label: text
text: Evans and Hett were the "stars" in the Club team. All three inside forwards, Evans, Woodward, and Allen, deserve praise. Owen Hughes on the wing was good at times, but occasionally inclined to be a little clumsy. Lammert was not so good, by comparison, although he made some good centres. One notable fault was that he did not always look to where he was passing.

label: text
text: Of the Club halves, Hett was the best, though Martin was not much behind him. As the Punjabi attack generally went by the wings, Mitchell had little to do at centre-half and therefore had no opportunity to distinguish him-self.

label: text
text: Lieut. Webb alone at centre-half for the Regiment, and the left half was also quite good. The forward ling was impressive, but lost as a result of the wingers running down too far so that they could not pass quickly enough.

label: paragraph_title
text: History of the Series

label: text
text: On Tuesday, as reported in this page yesterday, the "Club 2nd XI" went down to the soldiers' 2nd XI by three goals to nil. This is not the complete recent history of the encounters between these two teams.

label: text
text: Before the "official" season starting on October 7, the Punjabis beat the Club 4-0 on the Marina ground. Since that date, the Club have won, also by 4-0, and yesterday's victory makes the Hockey Club two matches up. In the season proper, there will be two more matches with the Punjabis on the Marina ground. Should the two teams be level at the end of the four matches, it may be necessary to play off a "final," the ground to be tossed for.

label: text
text:
Next Wednesday, the Club will meet an all-Navy XI instead of the Submarines as H.M.S. "Titania" is away.
The best matches of the season are those of the triangular tournament between the Army Navy and Club, won by the Club last season after being behind in the opening matches.

label: text
text: This season, the Navy is expected to be at great strength, and next Wednesday's match will give some of their best men an opportunity of playing together against the Club.

label: paragraph_title
text: HARBOUR SWIM.

label: text
text: CHINESE FIRST WITH BREAST STROKE.

label: text
text: INITIAL TRY WINS:

label: text
text: Using the breast stroke from start to finish, Wong Ping-fan won the harbour swim for Chinese (for the Challenge Cup presented by Mr. Mona Kensan of Measrs. Butterfield & Swire) in his first attempt in the annual race.

label: text
text: Last year's winner, Leung Titsang was a second, beaten by 200 yards. Tan Chiu-hin, who relied on back and trudgeon strokes, was a good third. Wong finished very strongly. Second and third were comparatively fresh when the race of just under a mile was over.

label: text
text: Conditions were very favourable, the breeze having died down and with only a slight current setting to East which did not trouble the competitors to any great extent.

label: text
text: Tan took the lead at first, followed by the winner who went to the front at any early stage and was never headed. Leung made his effort after having been in the water 22 minutes. His time last year was 31 mins. 22/8 secs. The finish was at the Praya wall outside the V.R.C.

text: The eight starters and their times were:—

label: paragraph_title
text: SUSPENDED!

label: text
text: ALLEGED LAWN TENNIS PAYMENTS

label: text
text: BELATED ACTION:

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: It is announced (by a message from Lahore) that the Council of the All-India Lawn Tennis Association has suspended S. M. Jacob until October 81, 1928 for contravening rules of the International Lawn Tennis Federation. This is apparently a sequel to incidents of April 20, April 24 and May 5.

label: text
text: [This year the British Lawn Tennis authorities have suspended several players for alleged receipt of expenses, or part expenses, for participation in certain tournaments. The trouble began with the visit of Mr. Helmore's team to Paris, where the players are stated to have violated rules by accepting the Paris Club's hospitality. Jacob claimed, directly or indirectly, that he was subject to the Indiana tennis council. He and other Indian players—who have resided in Britain for some years—gave an undertaking, under instructions from India, and the incident closed. The above cable now states that he is suspended.]

label: text
text:
HOBBS' SOOFTHES MUSLIM
WORLD

label: text
text: LONDON CARTOON OFIENDB

label: text
text: (Times of Ceylon)

label: text
text: London, October 3.

label: text
text: Jack Hobbs has earned another niche in the temple of fame.

label: text
text: Mr. Durd, head of the Almacdiyya Muslim Mission in London, has written to the Press saying that Hobbs has won favour with the whole of the Muslim world by soothing their feelings.

label: text
text:
It appears that when Hobbs was thrilling cricket enthusiasts in August, a London newspaper published a cartoon representing a gigantic figure of Hobbs overtopping pigmy statues of great figures in the world's history, amongst whom appeared Mohammed.
Mr. Dard elicited an expression of regret from the newspaper which this offended and he now publishes a letter he has received from Hobbs in the following terms:

label: text
text: "I am pained to know that the cartoon has offended the feelings of all Muslims."

label: text
text: After emphasising that he has no responsibility for newspaper cartoons, he says: "I am sorry that my success in cricket, which has been shared with me sport-loving people all over the world, has thus unfortunately become the occasion of wounding the religious susceptibility of any Muslims, who are my friends.

label: paragraph_title
text: TIME LIMIT.

label: text
text: (Router's Service.)

label: text
text: The Greek Government has sent an ultimatum to Bulgaria in connection with the frontier incident, giving a time limit of 48 hours and demanding an indemnity of 2,000,000 French francs, an expression of regret, and punishment of those responsible.

label: text
text: A semi-official statement in regard to the incident at Belles declares that a Greek soldier fired at a Bulgarian sentry who killed his assailant.

label: text
text: A fusilde followed.

label: text
text: THE WORD TO ACT:

label: text
text: The Premier, General Pangalos, states that troops are temporarily not entering Bulgaria but are only stationed along the frontier.

label: text
text: The initiative for further measures will be left to the commanding officer of the Third Army Corps.

label: text
text: EARLIER CABLES.

label: text
text: Comediently with Sofia amminging the signature to the Turco. Bulgarian Treaty of friendship and arbitration, Athens reports a Greece. Bulgarian frontier incident, namely that Bulgarian regulars attacked a Greek outpost at Belles, shooting a sentry and a captain dead. It says that subsequently the Bulgarists hoisted a white flag and explained that the firing was due to a misunderstanding. The Greek Government, however, despite the Bulgarian expressions of regret and the explanations made, is determined to throw full light on the incident and has ordered the Greek forces to advance to occupy certain points, whence it will be possible to ascertain the strength of the Bulgarian force.

label: text
text: TROOPS ORDERED TO BULOARM

label: text
text: According to an Athens telegram, the Government has decided to order Greek troops to advance into Bulgaria and occupy the town of Petritch, the headquarters of the Macedonian-Bulgarian committee, with the object of enforcing the Greek demands for satisfaction for the violation of Greek territory and the punishment of those responsible; also compensation to the relatives of those killed.

label: text
text:
AN ULTIMATUM THEATENED.
A report from Athens confirms the news that Greek detachments have been ordered to advance into Bulgarian territory to occupy Petritchi. It says that if the Greek demands are not promptly met probably an ultimatum will be addressed to Bulgaria. The Bulgarian Government proposes the formation of mixed commission of Greco-Bulgarian officers to investigate incident on the spot.

label: text
text: CREW'S PERLOUS RESCUE.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text:
Nova Scotia, October 21.
The Italian steamer "Ignazio Florio" from Montreal to Avonmouth has been abandoned and is sinking. The crew are safe aboard the steamer. "President Harding."

label: text
text: A message from New York reports that the "Ignazio Florio" suffered terribly from high seas in mid-Atlantic which swept over her. She lost her rudder and all the boats were smashed.

label: text
text: The second officer was swept overboard and the first officer had his leg broken. The ship was in danger of capsizing.

label: text
text: The "President Harding" stood by first. The attempt to get boats alongside was unsuccessful, but the crew of 37 were finally rescued.

label: paragraph_title

PROTECTING AMERICAN
LIVES.

label: text
text: DESTROYERS' MISSION

label: paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's American Service.)

label: text
text: Two American destroyers have been ordered to proceed from Gibraltar, where the American destroyer flotilla has just arrived, to Alexandria, for possible service at Syrian ports, and any action considered necessary for the protection of American lives and property from possible attacks by revolting Syrian tribesmen.

label: text
text: The request for destroyers came from the American Consul at Beirut.

label: text
text: State Department officials hope it will prove unnecessary to send vessels to Syria from Alexandria.

label: paragraph_title
text: HARD FACTS

label: text
text: BANKERS' APMITUDI

label: text
text: (Reuter's American Service.)

label: text
text: Washington, Oct. 21.

label: text
text: Further indications show that the Government is scrutinising all proposals for private loans by American financiers, to France were forthcoming after a Conference between President Coolidge and Mr. Mitchell, President of the National City Bank of New York.

label: text
text:
Mr. Mitchell subsequently stated that until France has settled her war, she should need to expect little sympathy from American bankers in the way of private loans.
He added that American banking officials were solidly behind the position taken up by the Government, and asserted that an American Banker attempting to float a private French loan in the present circumstances would only have a "faithy, hope and charity" proposition to offer the public.

text: The International Telegraph Conference has decided to appoint a committee to report on the matter of changes in code language. The present rules as regards code cypher will remain in force until the next conference three years hence.

label: text
text: The increase in telegraph rates has not yet come up for consideration at the plenary Conference but has been virtually adopted.
